findings.title: Normalize email addresses before matching the blocklist
findings.body: The blocklist lookup uses an exact, case-sensitive database comparison, and neither BlockedEmail nor the new validator normalizes the address. A blocked address such as `block@spamfromhome.org` can therefore register as `block@SpamFromHome.org`, even though email domains are case-insensitive and this is the same mailbox. Normalize both stored blocklist entries and incoming addresses using the application's email normalization rules before comparing them.

findings.title: Update match statistics atomically
findings.body: The match counter is updated with a read-modify-save sequence. If two requests match the same blocked address concurrently, both can read the same match_count and save the same incremented value, losing one match. The timestamp can also move backward when an older request saves last. Use an atomic database update or a row lock so concurrent validation attempts do not corrupt the blocklist statistics.
